title: Pinecrest Health SOC2/ISO Posture Review
next_steps: Maya to upload SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 cert to Redwood Trust Center (private link)
Liam to share KMS integration guide and sample config for customer-managed keys
Schedule technical deep-dive on SSO/SAML and RBAC mapping w/ Pinecrest infra team
Sofia to send list of required data residency regions and any contractual DPA addenda
action_items: Maya Chen; Upload SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 certificate to tenant trust center; 2025-11-14
Liam O'Connor; Prepare KMS/Multi-tenant key management doc and sample Terraform for Pinecrest; 2025-11-19
Sofia Martinez; Share Pinecrest required data residency regions and compliance addenda; 2025-11-18
Evan Brooks; Provide list of IP ranges and preferred VPC peering timelines; 2025-11-20
summary: Redwood (AE + SE) reviewed SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 posture for Pinecrest Health. Main discussion points: access to trust center and artifact sharing, controls mapping for SOC 2/ISO, RBAC/SSO (SAML) integration, audit logs retention and export, customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest, and data residency requirements. Agreed next steps include sharing certified reports in the trust center, a technical deep-dive on KMS and SAML, and providing a controls mapping template. Action items assigned and dates proposed.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right, thanks everyone for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE for Pinecrest. With me are Liam and Priya from our security and solution engineering team. Happy to hand it over to Rachel and the team to kick off — can you confirm objectives for today's call?
[00:12] Dr. Rachel Khan: Yeah hi Maya thanks. Goal is to validate Redwood's SOC 2 and ISO posture and understand how we can map controls to our internal checklist. Also we want to confirm SSO options, audit log retention, and if we can do customer-managed KMS.
[00:24] Evan Brooks: And timeline wise, we're aiming to complete vendor assessment by end of month so any docs you can surface quickly would help.
[00:31] Maya Chen: Awesome. We'll cover trust center access, where the reports live, controls mapping sample, and then Liam will dive into SSO/KMS and logging.
[00:38] Liam O'Connor: Quick note — transcription may be a little rough on acronyms, so apologies in advance.
[00:42] Sofia Martinez: no worries.
[00:44] Maya Chen: Okay first, SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 — Redwood has current attestations, we host them in the Trust Center. I can upload tenant-scoped links; we also have a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps our SOC 2 tests to common frameworks.
[01:00] Dr. Rachel Khan: When you say tenant-scoped link — is that for the hosted Redwood console or we need an NDA? We have to ensure only authorized compliance folks can access artifacts.
[01:08] Maya Chen: Good question. We can do two things: 1) provide a secure link in the Trust Center that requires SSO access (we support SAML/SSO for console), or 2) for particularly sensitive artifacts we can share via a signed NDA and a one-time secure link. Many health customers prefer the Trust Center link with RBAC.
[01:23] Sofia Martinez: Does the Trust Center also include the controls mapping for ISO? We need the mapping to Annex A controls.
[01:29] Priya Nair: Yes — our controls mapping doc includes SOC 2 criteria and a separate sheet that maps to ISO 27001 Annex A controls. It's a living doc and we can provide a version with redactions if necessary.
[01:39] Evan Brooks: Perfect. On data residency, Pinecrest requires PHI to stay in AWS us-east-2 and us-west-2 regions only. Can Redwood guarantee region pinning and contractual addendum for that?
[01:49] Liam O'Connor: We support region pinning for both hosted and dedicated. For hosted, we can pin requests to specific regional deployments; for dedicated and private deployments, it's straightforward. We can include data residency language in the DPA or an addendum. We'll need to align on where logs and backups are stored as well.
[02:04] Dr. Rachel Khan: About logs — what's your default retention and can we pull logs for audit? We need immutable audit logs for 12 months at minimum and export capability to our SIEM.
[02:15] Maya Chen: Default request/response logs are retained 90 days for hosted customers, but audit trail events (admin actions, config changes) are retained 12 months by default. We can extend retention as a paid add-on or via Dedicated. Exports to S3 and streaming to customer SIEM via syslog/HTTP SIEM endpoint are supported.
[02:34] Sofia Martinez: Is the audit log format documented? We need field mappings for our control evidence.
[02:38] Priya Nair: Yes we have a schema doc — I'll attach the logging schema and sample events. It includes timestamps, request ids, model, tenant id, user identity, and event type.
[02:49] Evan Brooks: On encryption, we prefer customer-managed keys (CMK) in AWS KMS. Can Redwood support CMK for model artifacts and persisted data?
[02:58] Liam O'Connor: Short answer: yes for certain artifacts. For hosted multi-tenant workloads, we currently support envelope encryption where customer data can be encrypted with a customer-managed wrapping key — we can integrate with AWS KMS (and GCP KMS/Azure Key Vault for other clouds) via a KMS integration. For dedicated or private deployments you can bring your own key material.
[03:17] Dr. Rachel Khan: Important: we need a key-rotation policy and proof that keys are not stored in plaintext anywhere. Also, we require HSM-backed keys if possible.
[03:25] Liam O'Connor: We use provider KMS which is HSM-backed (e.g., AWS KMS uses HSM). We don't retain plaintext key material in our systems; we store references and use envelope encryption. Rotation can be handled by customer or we can coordinate rotation windows — we'll document a recommended rotation process and support zero-downtime rotation patterns.
[03:42] Maya Chen: Quick interjection — we should note any deviations from SOC 2 tests, e.g., for hosted multi-tenant customers where some physical controls are managed by cloud provider; we include that in the mapping.
[03:52] Dr. Rachel Khan: Good, call that out.
[03:54] [05:00] Liam O'Connor: SSO — we support SAML 2.0, OIDC, and SCIM for provisioning. For RBAC we have role templates and allow mapping to your SAML attributes. Typical mapping: "redwood:role" claim mapped to RBAC role; we also support attribute-based access controls for environment-level restrictions.
[05:20] Evan Brooks: Do you support SCIM for automatic user provisioning and group sync?
[05:23] Liam O'Connor: Yes, SCIM v2.0 for user/group sync. Provisioning events are auditable in the admin audit logs.
[05:30] Sofia Martinez: On RBAC, can we restrict access so only a small set of users can view logs and artifacts? Our compliance team cannot have read access to production data — they only need configuration and control evidence.
[05:42] Priya Nair: Yes, you can create custom roles — e.g., "compliance.viewer" that grants artifact and report read access but blocks request payload read. We can show a demo of role creation and policy examples in the follow-up deep-dive.
[05:56] Dr. Rachel Khan: For controls mapping — our infosec team wants to map Redwood controls to our SOC 2+ISO matrix and also have evidence IDs we can cite. Does Redwood provide test evidence artifacts and dates (like test window and auditor)?
[06:10] Maya Chen: The Trust Center artifacts include the auditor statement, report period, and then for controls mapping we include descriptions of evidence types (e.g. configuration snapshot, policy docs, log extracts) and for some items we can provide sample evidence or redacted extracts.
[06:23] Sofia Martinez: How about penetration test reports? Are those available?
[06:27] Liam O'Connor: We do internal pentests and have third-party assessments for the platform — high-level summaries are in the Trust Center. Full reports require NDA and specific request; some customers opt to receive a redacted summary and remediation timeline.
[06:40] Evan Brooks: Compliance question — does Redwood have a dedicated SOC contact for notifications like incident response? We need an SLA for incident notifications and post-incident reports.
[06:50] Maya Chen: Yes we have a security incident response process; incident notification SLAs are in our SOC 2 controls and can be included in an enterprise addendum. Standard practice: initial notification within 24 hours for high-severity incidents and a detailed report within X days — we can put precise SLA language into the contract.
[07:06] Dr. Rachel Khan: Can you show an example of the controls mapping now?
[07:10] Priya Nair: Sure — I'll share my screen. (brief screen pass, some background noise)
[07:18] [07:30] Priya Nair: On the left we list SOC 2 CC criteria columns; middle column is Redwood control description; right column maps to ISO Annex A controls. For example, "CC6: Logical and physical access controls" maps to A.9 and A.8 in ISO. Evidence type: IAM configuration, MFA enforcement logs, periodic access review artifacts.
[07:48] Dr. Rachel Khan: For access reviews, do you have attestations or automated reports we can download?
[07:52] Priya Nair: We generate quarterly access review reports; we can provide the report metadata and hashes as evidence. Automated exports can be scheduled into your S3.
[08:03] Evan Brooks: We may want to run a short benchmark to validate latency and to test regional routing. Is that something Redwood can support? We want to include perf as part of vendor evaluation.
[08:12] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely — we can run a small-run benchmark from us-east-2 to show warm vs cold latencies. For SOC assessment, perf isn't required but we can include it in the POC scoping.
[08:22] Sofia Martinez: Back to encryption — can you provide the KMS log events that show key usage? We need to correlate key usage to data access events.
[08:30] Liam O'Connor: We emit key usage logs (where supported by provider). For AWS KMS, CloudTrail events show Encrypt/Decrypt calls and we can surface a subset as part of audit exports. We'll document exact CloudTrail event types and sample outputs.
[08:45] Dr. Rachel Khan: Any limitations around backups and snapshot encryption? We enforce encryption at rest for backups and would like confirmation snapshots are also encrypted with the same customer-managed key.
[08:55] Priya Nair: Snapshots are encrypted; for dedicated/private we can ensure snapshots are encrypted with your CMK. For hosted multi-tenant, snapshots containing mixed tenancy metadata are encrypted using our wrapping key but you can request exportable backups under dedicated contract. We'll call out that nuance in the controls mapping (where cloud-provider responsibilities intersect).
[09:18] [09:30] Maya Chen: We're mindful of shared responsibilities — we will clearly mark which controls are "Redwood", "Cloud Provider", or "Customer" in the mapping doc.
[09:39] Evan Brooks: For audit purposes, can we run an on-demand export of request logs for a given tenant and timeframe?
[09:46] Liam O'Connor: Yes — exports are supported; for hosted we have a 90-day rolling default but we can do ad-hoc exports for longer windows if you request them and we can ingest into your S3 or SIEM. For Dedicated, retention is configurable.
[09:58] Sofia Martinez: What's the process for a deeper technical review? I'd like to invite our infra folks and a PKI engineer next time.
[10:05] Maya Chen: We'll schedule a technical deep-dive. Liam, Priya, can you propose times and an agenda?
[10:10] Liam O'Connor: Yep — propose an agenda: 1) KMS integration and key rotation; 2) SAML/SCIM mapping and RBAC demo; 3) Audit log schema and export walkthrough; 4) Controls mapping Q&A.
[10:22] Dr. Rachel Khan: Sounds good. Also please include a copy of your penetration test summary and scope so we can note that in our risk assessment.
[10:29] Priya Nair: We'll include the redacted pentest summary and remediation timeline.
[10:33] [10:40] Maya Chen: All right wrapping up — to recap: Maya uploads reports to Trust Center and shares access link; Liam shares KMS guide and sample configs; Priya attaches controls mapping and logging schema; Pinecrest to provide data residency list and IP ranges. We'll follow up with a technical deep-dive next week.
[10:57] Evan Brooks: Thanks everyone — that timeline works.
[11:01] Dr. Rachel Khan: Thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[11:03] Sofia Martinez: Thanks all.
[11:05] Maya Chen: Thanks — we'll get notes and artifacts out by Friday.
[11:10] [END OF RECORDING]
